newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks open bourse trade slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: German stocks open bourse trade slightly lower.

text.p: The DAX index of 30 German blue-chip shares opened bourse trading lower on Wednesday as the index fell to around levels seen in its electronic IBIS counterpart, with support from a stronger dollar and firmer German debt.
In early bourse trading the DAX stood at 3,577.08 points, down 18.07 points or half a percent, but still around the high levels seen in recent days.
Meanwhile the June DAX future contract was up 17.5 points at 3,582.5 points.

"The dollar is picking up and that is helping to support the market. To be honest I think we need to see a bit of profit-taking, a bit of consolidation. The market feels a bit toppy at the moment," a trader said.

The market of late has been trading in or around record levels and traders said there was evidence that of a touch of vertigo at these heights without solid fundamentals to back up the bullish sentiment.

The telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom was the main focus of attention in early bourse as one of the main losers, following newspaper reports that Bonn might consider selling some its Telekom shares to help pare back its budget deficit.
The paper reported that the Bonn government wants to sell a portion of its nearly 75 percent stake in Telekom this year as part of efforts to pare back the budget deficit.
The news drove the shares nearly four and a half percent lower at one point in electronic trade, but the share recovered somewhat and was trading at 39.15 marks, down 98 pfennigs, or 2.44 percent.

"I think that today we are going to see a Telekom bourse, but the market is proving resistant," a Frankfurt trader said, adding that volumes were enormous early on, but that 38 marks was proving to be a point of massive resistance.
The trader said that if it was true that Bonn was planning to sell off the share, then the earnings potential for the Telekom share was limited.
However, dealers insisted that the fundamental figures for Telekom remained good. "All in all, I think the market could well absorb a big block of Telekom shares," the trader said.
Other traders were sceptical whether Bonn would actually bring the shares to market in the end. "We're also seeing more buyers than sellers at the lower levels," said one trader.

Bank stocks were also in favour in early bourse as reports that NordLB and Bankgesellschaft Berlin said they wanted to begin talks on a merger fuelled speculation about mergers among the larger banks.
Deutsche Bank rose 1.51 percent in electronic trade, but came back in early bourse to stand at 97.65 marks, up 35 pfennigs or around 0.35 percent.
